strengths: The method addresses an important practical problem: distilling large image datasets without expensive bilevel optimization. Combining representative feature targets with class-specific BatchNorm regularization is a plausible and useful approach.

Table I reports consistent improvements over the strengthened SRe²L reproduction. On ImageNet-1K, accuracy increases from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100 images per class. Evaluation covers three datasets and four distillation budgets.

The authors transparently report substantial improvements from reproducing SRe²L and disclose the associated hyperparameter changes. Component ablations, regularization sensitivity experiments, and supplementary implementation details help assess the method. Its major methodological dependencies are appropriately credited.
Table II demonstrates useful transfer within the ResNet family, while the image examples provide qualitative evidence of increased within-class variety.
weaknesses: The central contribution is insufficiently distinguished from standard clustering. Equation 4 approximates a single empirical distribution with a limited number of support points. For squared Euclidean 2-Wasserstein cost and freely optimized masses, the stated unregularized objective is equivalent to k-means quantization. The paper neither explains this connection nor compares against k-means feature targets using identical image recovery. Consequently, the added value of the Wasserstein formulation remains unclear.

The ablations attribute most improvement to class-specific BatchNorm statistics. In Table III, holding cross-entropy and class-specific BatchNorm fixed, adding the barycenter loss changes accuracy from 64.0% to 63.9% on ImageNette, 41.3% to 42.1% on Tiny ImageNet, and 37.4% to 37.9% on ImageNet-1K. These modest effects, tested only at 10 images per class, do not adequately substantiate the central explanation that Wasserstein matching drives the gains. A comparison against MMD under the same feature extractor and regularization is also missing.

There is an unresolved mismatch between the optimized distribution and the delivered dataset. Equation 3 and Algorithms 2–3 learn nonuniform support weights, but Algorithm 1 outputs only images, and their use in student sampling or training is not specified. Moreover, the text claims entropy regularization, while the appendix presents unregularized transport objectives without specifying the entropy coefficient, initialization, or numerical stopping settings. These omissions affect both interpretation and reproducibility of the core component.

The efficiency claim lacks a sufficient comparison. Table IV measures only one synthetic-image update on 64×64 ImageNette, without a baseline or accounting for feature extraction and barycenter computation. The supplementary 14-hour ImageNet experiment does not provide a stage breakdown or matched timing against SRe²L, so preservation of distribution-matching efficiency is not established.

Broader claims exceed the demonstrated scope. Cross-architecture results lack a competing-method baseline, and ImageNet accuracy drops to 7.5% on ViT-Tiny at 10 images per class. All three datasets are ImageNet-derived, and benchmark comparisons cover methods only through 2023, leaving the claimed generality and state-of-the-art standing for ICCV 2025 insufficiently supported.
